issue.title: Go SDK: a pointer spec field cannot be set from a literal
issue.body:
### What happens

`airflow.DagSpec` and `airflow.TaskSpec` carry 9 pointer fields, so that a value an author
sets explicitly is distinguishable from one left unset — a `bool` whose default comes from
Airflow config, such as `catchup`, is the clearest case.

Go does not allow taking the address of a literal, so the obvious spelling does not compile:

```go
dag := airflow.Dag("etl", airflow.DagSpec{Catchup: &false})  // invalid operand
```

An author has to name a variable for every such field:

```go
catchup := false
dag := airflow.Dag("etl", airflow.DagSpec{Catchup: &catchup})
```

### What would fix it

Go 1.26's `new(expr)`:

```go
dag := airflow.Dag("etl", airflow.DagSpec{Catchup: new(false)})
```

### Why this is deferred rather than done

`go-sdk/go.mod` is on `go 1.25.0`. Go 1.26 was released in February 2026, which is too new
to require of everyone who builds a Go bundle, so the floor is not being raised for this.
Decided while reviewing #73936.

An `airflow.Ptr[T]` generic helper was considered and rejected there: the pointer
transformation is the language's job, not the SDK's.

### Acceptance

- [ ] Go 1.26 is an acceptable minimum for the Go SDK.
- [ ] `go-sdk/go.mod` raised to it.
- [ ] `new(expr)` used in the Dag authoring docs and examples, so the spelling an author
      copies is the short one.

---
Drafted-by: Claude Code (Opus 5) (no human review before posting)

comments.body:
> [@henry3260](https://github.com/henry3260) can I take this up?

Thanks @Rachit-Gandhi, but this can't be picked up yet, the fix needs Go 1.26 (`new(expr)`), and the go-sdk is still on 1.25 with no plan to raise it for now. Since it's blocked on that version decision, it's not a good first issue. I'll keep it assigned to myself and revisit once 1.26 is an acceptable minimum.
